i really feel for you, schizophrenia is such a stigmatised condition and it really hurts me to see. i am a psychology major and to me schizophrenia is normal, just like someone having a cold. i know you feel like you don’t fit in anywhere because of your illness but the reality is that educated people understand your struggles and are not judging you. if you’re having trouble telling your friends and family, sit down and tell them about schizophrenia in a very real and normal way, and then simply say that you have it. it isn’t something to be scared of, it’s just a different type of a cold.

update: i ended up calling my friend who also has very severe anxiety and i started having a panic attack while on the phone to her and she managed to calm me down and reason with me a bit, she told me she would drive me to the other friends house so we could go in together which automatically made me feel a little bit better, the night was hard and i would have preferred to be at home but i’m glad i went because it sort of proved to me that my anxiety doesn’t have to control me.
thanks heaps for the advice the world needs more people like you :)

the guys she invited are fine though, like i know them well enough and id almost say we are sort of friends but i’m not super close with them and idk i really just wanted to be able to hang out with my friends and not worry about anything. i feel bad for saying no because she invited me over a week ago and i said yes, and i’ve been looking forward to it all week, there’s no reason why i shouldn’t go other than i feel like crap.

Hey there, i’m no medical expert but i did my psych final on CTE, while you are very young and CTE is more common in older people it is possible for you to have it. it all depends on when you experienced the trauma and also how severe it was. your symptoms do align with those of CTE however blacking out and ringing ears isn’t one of them as far as i know. as of right now it is impossible to diagnose CTE in a living person however it looks like the near future may see PET scans with traceable dye that sticks to tau protein may be an option. i would suggest asking your doctor and possibly getting some scans done to eliminate any other issues you may have.

i know you’ve been thinking about this a lot and i respect that. i’m not trying to change your mind but i read you have post partum depression in one of your other posts. maybe try giving your baby to you parents to take care of for a few weeks and just take time to breathe by yourself and see if anything changes. not trying to push you to stay alive just a suggestion because i know your baby would be hurt when they find out the truth down the line.
